text:
Base case fair value: CHF 0.89 / share. Current market: CHF 4.35 (mid June 2026). Apparent downside: −80 %.
But the number to remember is not −80 %. The 80 % apparent gap is what the market is paying for three catalysts the base case deliberately excludes: (1) a residual claim on the ring fenced SARL assets (aprocitentan / selatogrel / cenerimod), (2) a QUVIVIQ blockbuster trajectory north of CHF 600 M peak, (3) equity optionality on the J&J convertible. The reconciled fair value therefore sits anywhere in CHF 0.9 – 6.6 per share depending on how one weights those catalysts. A “Base + modest SARL residual (CHF 400 M)” reads at CHF ~2.5 / share.

title: Results
text:
What the valuation rides on

Two variables dominate, nearly tied, the SARL residual assumption (0 vs CHF 400 M swings the model from CHF 0.89 to CHF 2.48 / share) and QUVIVIQ peak sales (±30 % swings from CHF 0.09 to CHF 1.69). Third is the QUVIVIQ operating margin (±5 pp). Discount rate is a mid tier lever; lucerastat peak sales and PoS matter but do not move the needle on their own.
Critical read of the tornado: no single variable at its stress case reaches the current market price. Closing the gap requires multiple positive assumptions simultaneously, that is the market’s implicit bet.

To reach the current CHF 4.35 with QUVIVIQ alone requires peak sales CHF ~1 000-1 100 M and a discount rate at the low end of the WACC range (9-10 %). That is not implausible, descheduling in the US, IDSIQ label enhancement, and pediatric approval, if all three land, plausibly get QUVIVIQ into that territory, but each is a separate probabilistic event.

title: Results
text:
Verdict
The market is not wrong; the base case is not wrong. They price different things.
The base case values only the parent owned assets, uses industry standard Phase 2 to approval and Phase 3 to approval probabilities, and applies a conservative peak sales estimate to a genuinely differentiated but uncertain commercial asset. It answers the question: “If none of the three catalysts materialise, what is Idorsia worth?” The answer is CHF ~0.9 / share.
The market answers the different question: “What is Idorsia worth on a probability weighted basis, including some credit for the SARL reversion and for QUVIVIQ becoming a genuine blockbuster?” The reconciled fair value in that framework sits somewhere in CHF 2.5 – 5 / share. The market is at CHF 4.35, the upper end of that range.
My reconciled personal read: at CHF 4.35, IDIA is pricing in a material SARL residual plus a QUVIVIQ trajectory noticeably above the CHF 600 M I use as base. That is a fairly optimistic combination which is not irrational, but leaves limited margin of safety at the current level. It is not an obvious buy at these levels; it is not obviously a sell either. It is a name whose fair value critically depends on things that will be known in the next 18-24 months, the CCR6 PoC readout (Q4 2026), the US QUVIVIQ commercial trajectory, and progress on repaying the SARL notes.

title: Results
text:
Limitations

All figures are constrained by the quality of the peak sales, PoS and discount rate inputs.
Peak sales for the three Phase 2 candidates are placeholders and drive their negative rNPVs. A positive CCR6 PoC readout at Q4 2026 would materially reshape those figures.
The J&J convertible is treated as pure debt at its CHF ~11.55 strike (deep OTM at current prices). Rerating would turn it into an equity dilution event.
Working capital and capex are netted to zero; tax proxied by EBIT margin; product outcomes are assumed independent.
The SARL contingent liability to J&J (30 % of aprocitentan proceeds + 10 % each of selatogrel and cenerimod) is disclosed but not fully modelled, a known refinement.
Modelling conventions (mid year discount, 8 year QUVIVIQ ramp) are documented in Methodology §Modelling conventions.

Don’t read the CHF 0.89 as a price target. Read the sourcing and the scenarios. Every input is traceable to a public document, every scenario has an explicit narrative, and every CHF of the gap between the model and the market can be tied to a specific bet.

Full computation trail: interactive notebook | methodology | source on GitHub.

title: Methodology
text: This page describes how each pipeline product is modelled, how probability weighting is applied, and how the product rNPVs are aggregated into an enterprise value and a per share value.

title: Methodology
text:
The rNPV formula
For each product, the risk adjusted NPV is:
\(rNPV = \sum_{t=T_0}^{T_{end}} \frac{CF_t \times PoS_{cumulative}}{(1+r)^t} \; - \; \sum_{t=0}^{T_0-1} \frac{DevCost_t}{(1+r)^t}\)$
Where:

\(CF_t\) = operating cash flow in year \(t\) = \(Sales_t \times \text{OpMargin}\)
\(PoS_{cumulative}\) = cumulative probability that the product reaches the market from its current phase
\(r\) = discount rate (biotech WACC)
\(DevCost_t\) = remaining clinical development cost in year \(t\)
\(T_0\) = expected launch year, \(T_{end}\) = end of exclusivity window (post patent cliff)

title: Methodology
text:
Probability of success (PoS)
Phase to market probabilities are sourced from published academic benchmarks (Wong, Siah & Lo 2019, MIT; BIO Industry Analysis reports). Indicative values used as starting points:



Current phase
PoS to market




Phase I
~10 %


Phase II
~15–20 %


Phase III
~50–60 %


Filed
~85–90 %


Marketed / approved
100 %



Exact values used in the model are stored in src/assumptions.py with source citations for each product.

title: Methodology
text:
Revenue curve
For each product we model annual sales as:

Ramp phase, linear (or S curve) buildup over ~5–7 years from launch to peak.
Peak phase, plateau at the estimated peak sales figure.
Patent cliff, sharp decline (typically –80 % to –90 % over 1–2 years) at loss of exclusivity.

Peak sales are constructed bottom up where possible:
\[\text{Peak Sales} = \text{Target patient population} \times \text{Penetration rate} \times \text{Annual price}\]
Every number is sourced (annual report, published analyst estimates, epidemiology literature) and the source is recorded next to the value in assumptions.py.

title: Methodology
text:
Operating margin and cash flow
Sales are converted to operating cash flow using an EBIT margin appropriate for a specialty biotech at maturity (indicative range: 25–40 %). The margin is sourced/hypothesised and disclosed. Working capital and capex are treated as netting to zero over the forecast horizon (standard rNPV simplification, discussed in Limitations).

title: Methodology
text:
Development costs
For products not yet on the market, the remaining clinical development cost (Phase III trials, filing) is subtracted as an unweighted expense in the years before launch (i.e. spent regardless of approval outcome). Indicative per phase costs are sourced from published benchmarks.

title: Methodology
text:
Discount rate
A biotech appropriate WACC in the 11–13 % range is used. The base case is set in assumptions.py and the value is stress tested in the sensitivity section.

title: Methodology
text:
Modelling conventions
Two non obvious choices sit under the rNPV that would produce materially different numbers if flipped. Both are documented here for transparency.

Discounting convention: mid year
Cash flows in year \(t\) are discounted by \((1+r)^{-(t - t_0 + 0.5)}\), the mid year convention. This is the textbook rNPV default: cash is assumed to flow evenly through the year, so the current year cash flow gets half a year of discounting. Two alternatives exist:








Convention
Formula
Effect on base case (CHF/share)




Start of year
\((1+r)^{-(t - t_0)}\)
~ +6 % higher (no discount on t₀ CF)


Mid year (used here)
\((1+r)^{-(t - t_0 + 0.5)}\)
base


End of year
\((1+r)^{-(t - t_0 + 1)}\)
~ −6 % lower (full year of discount on t₀ CF)



The convention is exposed as a keyword argument on discount_factors() in rnpv.py so it can be flipped in one line for stress testing.


QUVIVIQ ramp trajectory: 8 years to peak
The model interpolates linearly from the last anchored sales figure (CHF 200 M guidance for 2026) to the peak of CHF 600 M by 2030, a 4-year interpolation from the anchor, or an 8-year ramp counted from the 2022 launch year. This produces the sequence 200 → 300 → 400 → 500 → 600 (2026-2030), consistent with the ~+50 % YoY growth Idorsia has been delivering and guides for 2026.
An earlier draft used ramp_years = 6 (peak in 2028), which would imply 200 → 400 → 600 in two years, 100 % then 50 % YoY growth. Defensible only under an aggressive combined US descheduling + pediatric approval + European reimbursement bull case. The current setting is deliberately more conservative and can be retightened via the tornado / heatmap.


What is NOT modelled
Consistent with the “order of magnitude” tool ambition:

Taxes, subsumed into the operating margin. A separate effective tax layer would trim EV by ~10–20 %.
Working capital and capex, netted to zero over the forecast horizon.
Product outcome correlation, treated as independent (no portfolio effect).
J&J convertible optionality, the CHF 335 M convertible loan is treated as pure debt at its ~CHF 11.55 strike. Rerating toward the strike would introduce dilution.
SARL cash flow priorities, the ring fenced debt at Idorsia Investments SARL is excluded from the parent bridge in the base case; the residual reversion to the parent is set to zero and stressed only in scenarios.

title: Methodology
text:
Aggregation
\[EV = \sum_{i \in products} rNPV_i + \text{NetCash}\]
\[\text{Value per share} = \frac{EV}{\text{Shares outstanding}}\]
Net cash and shares outstanding are taken from the most recent Idorsia balance sheet and share count disclosures.

title: Methodology
text:
Sensitivity
The model is stress tested along the axes that dominate rNPV in practice:

Discount rate (10 % → 14 %)
PoS of the lead clinical candidate (±20 %)
Peak sales of the top revenue driver (±30 %)
A tornado chart ranks the sensitivities.

title: Methodology
text:
Limitations

rNPV is an order of magnitude tool, not a precise valuation.
Assumes independence of product level outcomes (no portfolio correlation modelling).
Working capital and capex are netted to zero.
No explicit tax treatment beyond an EBIT margin proxy.
Sensitive to peak sales assumptions, which are inherently uncertain.

title: rNPV Valuation, Idorsia (SIX: IDIA)
text: What is the fair per share value of Idorsia, a Swiss biotech (SIX: IDIA), when its clinical pipeline is valued product by product using phase specific probabilities of success, and how does that fair value compare to the current market capitalisation?

title: rNPV Valuation, Idorsia (SIX: IDIA)
text:
Summary
Method: Risk adjusted NPV. Each pipeline product is projected as a revenue curve (ramp → peak → plateau → patent cliff), converted into operating cash flows via an EBIT margin, discounted at a biotech WACC, and probability weighted using phase specific success rates from published benchmarks. Enterprise value = sum of product rNPVs + net cash. Per share value = EV / shares outstanding.
Scope: QUVIVIQ (daridorexant, marketed), lucerastat (Phase 3, Fabry disease), and three Phase 2 candidates (CCR6, CXCR7, CXCR3 antagonists). The three assets transferred in 2025 to the ring fenced Idorsia Investments SARL (aprocitentan, selatogrel, cenerimod) are deliberately excluded from the base case and treated as an option like residual, see Methodology §Structural note.
Main finding: Base case fair value CHF 0.89 / share vs market CHF 4.35 (mid June 2026). The ~80 % apparent gap is not a claim IDIA is overvalued 5×, it decomposes cleanly into three catalysts the base case excludes: (1) SARL residual value, (2) QUVIVIQ blockbuster trajectory, (3) J&J convertible optionality. Reconciled fair value across scenarios: CHF 0.9 – 6.6 / share. See the full note in Results.
